name: MAIN STREET (CANDIDATE)
note: Room 2. The hub, and the most-visited screen in the game. LOOK and LISTEN lines are verbatim from docs/05-examine-layer.md; repeat variants and verb overrides are verbatim from docs/13-room-02-content.md; the four exits from docs/14-room-02-exits.md. Nothing on this screen was written by anyone implementing it.

LOOK_AT.say: A dog with the settled look of an animal that has outlasted several owners.
repeat: He has not moved. He has the air of a creature waiting for the town to finish.
He is looking at me. I have nothing to offer and he knows it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Breathing. Contented. He is the only solvent resident of Consolation.
repeat: Still contented. Still solvent.
Nothing. He has gone to sleep in the middle of my attention.

overrides.PICK_UP: I am not picking up a dog I have not been introduced to.

ordinary.note: PHASE 1.5E: THE BOARD IS PLATE. The freestanding notice board -- rough timber, two posts on the boardwalk, a plank cap, the ordinary pinned papers -- was painted into the environment by the Region A structural repair (art/staging/room-02/repair-a/repair-op.json, street-candidate-03). The ORDINARY state draws nothing over it; the plate IS the ordinary board.

funeral.note: Act III: ONLY the changed paper -- the Phase 1.5B aged funeral sheet, pinned centre-top on the SAME physical board (a sheet-only overlay, no board pixels). No copy invented; the notice's words are the LOOK line's. Set by doc 48's S2.

LOOK_AT.say: Claims for sale, claims disputed, a lost dog, and a man offering to write letters home for those who cannot. He is doing better than anyone.
repeat: The lost dog notice has been up six weeks. The dog is on this street.
Four claims for sale today. There were three yesterday.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper, in wind. A great deal of it.
repeat: Paper. Still a great deal of it.
One corner has come loose and is knocking. It will do that until somebody dies.

overrides.PICK_UP: They belong to the town. I have read them four times, which I consider a form of ownership.
overrides.OPEN: They are already facing outward. That is the whole design.

LOOK_AT.say: A trough. Three inches of water and a great deal of ambition.
repeat: The water has not improved.
Three inches. I have measured it with a stick, which is the most scientific act performed in Consolation this year.

LISTEN_TO.say: Something is living in it. I have decided not to pursue this.
repeat: It is still in there. It has moved.
We have reached an understanding.

overrides.USE: I have drunk from it once. The once is doing a great deal of work in that sentence.
overrides.OPEN: It is a trough. It is entirely open. It is nothing but open.

LOOK_AT.say: The tallest thing in Consolation, and the only building that is as deep as it is tall.
repeat: Still the only honest building on the horizon.
Somebody built that properly. I should like to meet them and I suspect they have left.

LISTEN_TO.say: The bell is a half-step flat.
repeat: Half a step. Every time.
I have begun to hear it correctly in my head before it rings, which is the first sign of something.
then: It has been struck by hand for six years by a man who does not care.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is four hundred yards away and approximately forty feet tall. I admire the ambition of the instruction.
overrides.TALK_TO: I am not going to shout at a church from a street.

weathered.note: PHASE 1.5G: REBUILT LETTER BY LETTER (doc 36 Q123). 1.5F rotated the whole crop level and the letters still stepped up and down the way the old angled board left them, which is what reads as crooked. Each authored glyph is now MOVED by whole pixels against its line's measured slant -- never rotated, never resampled -- so both lines sit on one row: baseline spread 6 px -> 2 on CONSOLATION, 7 px -> 1 on IMPROVEMENT COMPANY. This is the base state: the same seeded dulling and flaking as Phase 1.5.

gilt.note: Act III. Doc 05 Part Two-B: 'Fresh gilt on the lettering.' PHASE 1.5G: cut from the SAME rebuilt lettering as the weathered state, so the two cannot differ in position or angle by a pixel. Set by doc 48's S2.

repeat: Gilt. Actual gilt. In a town where the road is a suggestion.
Painted twice, and the second time by a better man than the first.
then: It is the only sign in town that has been painted twice.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is the quietest building on the street and it is always full.
repeat: Nothing. Still full.
Nothing at all. Whatever they do in there, they do it without raising their voices.

overrides.PULL: It is screwed on. Thoroughly. Somebody paid for it to be screwed on.
overrides.TALK_TO: I have spoken to the building it is attached to. It went badly and I have not recovered.

repeat: Six inches. I have never been so aware of six inches.
The boards are good. Somebody spent money on the one thing that keeps a man out of the road.
then: In Consolation, this is the difference between a gentleman and a prospector.

LISTEN_TO.say: Loose board, third from the end. Everyone in town steps over it without thinking.
repeat: Third from the end. Still loose.
It has a note. B flat, roughly. I have decided not to tell anyone.

overrides.PULL: The loose board declines to come up. It is loose recreationally, not professionally.
overrides.PUSH: Third from the end. Up an inch, down an inch. Nobody has ever fixed it.

LOOK_AT.say: Mud, the full width of the street and six inches deep.
repeat: The same mud. I have begun to recognize individual portions of it.
That portion I have named. I will not be sharing the name.
then: The boardwalk is six inches high. Somebody worked that out.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is mud, and it is being mud.
repeat: Nothing new.
Nothing new. I want that understood.

overrides.PICK_UP: I have picked up some mud. I am now a man holding mud, in a street, at night.

LOOK_AT.say: Gold country. Everyone here has looked at these hills for years and seen a number.
repeat: Still gold country. Still no gold.
They are the same hills as yesterday. I check.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. They are extremely large and they are not doing anything.
repeat: Nothing. Still large.
Nothing. I should be alarmed if there were.

overrides.USE: I would not know where to begin, and neither would they.

LOOK_AT.say: Half this street is two stories tall in front and one story deep.
repeat: Still two stories of nothing. I keep hoping the back will have arrived.
I have counted. Six fronts, six sheds, one town.
then: Consolation is a stage set people have moved into.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind. There is a great deal of nothing behind half of these.
repeat: The same nothing. It is a very consistent nothing.
Nothing. I have stopped expecting otherwise and I am the better for it.

overrides.PUSH: I have pushed the front of a building. It did not fall over, which is more than I expected.
overrides.PULL: If I pull hard enough the entire town comes down, and I have not settled how I feel about that.

LOOK_AT.say: The Bountiful Nugget. Batwing doors, which swing both ways, and which I suspect is the whole philosophy of the establishment.
repeat: Somebody spent money on those doors and on nothing else. I have looked.
The Nugget. It is bountiful in the way that a promise is bountiful.

LISTEN_TO.say: Talk, glasses, and a piano that is flat in one place. I could put it right in four minutes and nobody has asked me.
repeat: Still flat. C-sharp. It is going to be C-sharp for the rest of my life.
Somebody in there has told the same story four times and it has grown twice.

overrides.CLOSE: They swing. Closing them is a temporary opinion.
overrides.TALK_TO: I would have to go in. Going in costs money.
overrides.PULL: They swing outward, inward, and for some time afterwards.

LOOK_AT.say: CONSOLATION IMPROVEMENT COMPANY. The door is a great deal heavier than the building requires.
repeat: Everyone who goes in comes out pleased. I have watched eleven men do it.
Three storeys from here. I have been round the back and it is one.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is the quietest doorway on the street and it is never still.
repeat: Nothing. Somebody is always going in.
Nothing at all. Not one raised voice in eleven weeks.

overrides.PUSH: It opens inward, which is a decision somebody made.
overrides.TALK_TO: I have spoken to the man behind that door. I came away with a map and I am no longer certain what I gave him.
overrides.CLOSE: It closes on its own, slowly, and without a sound. Somebody paid for that too.

LOOK_AT.say: The Consolation Clarion. One press, one man, and the front page of every issue for twelve years has been about a hole nobody can find.
repeat: The door is open. The door is always open. He is desperate for somebody to say something quotable.
There is a bill in the window advertising the Clarion, printed by the Clarion, on the Clarion's press.

LISTEN_TO.say: The press. It knocks on the return stroke, and it has knocked for years.
repeat: Knocking. Still knocking.
He is talking to himself in there. He is doing both sides of an interview.

overrides.TALK_TO: If I say anything within forty feet of that door it will be in print by four o'clock.
overrides.CLOSE: He would only open it again, and then write about it.

LOOK_AT.say: The road out to the diggings. Worn a foot deep by boots — which is more dirt than anybody out there has shifted on purpose.
repeat: Two miles. It looks further in the morning and considerably further at night.
Somewhere down there is forty feet of mud that is legally mine.

LISTEN_TO.say: Boots. A great many of them, going out. It is the most cheerful sound in Consolation and it happens at six in the morning.
repeat: Nothing at the moment. They are all out there.
Nothing coming back yet. They come back quiet.

overrides.CLOSE: I have considered it. Several of us have.

exits.name: THE ASSAY OFFICE
exits.note: Doc 20's graph: the sixth enterable facade. Room 5 was composed, wired with sixteen lines and audited three times while nothing on Main Street opened onto it. Marked stub because doc 05's Room 2 does not script this door and its examine lines are not written; inventing them would be worse than the honest gap. The rect is the door and its step. The lot was drawn BOARDED with tools leaning across it, which is ruling 19b in the other direction -- art asserting a building this exit contradicts -- and it now has a door, clean glass and a worn step, and nothing else. It is still the plainest front on the street.

LOOK_AT.say: The assay office. A door, a step, and one window. It is the only front on this street that is not selling itself.
repeat: No sign. Everybody knows where it is and nobody needs telling twice.
The step is worn pale in the middle and nowhere else. They come, they stand, they go.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is the quietest working building in Consolation.
repeat: Nothing. A pen, possibly. I may be inventing the pen.
Nothing at all. Whatever is decided in there is decided without discussion.

shut.note: As the room composes. Winnie's door is shut because Winnie is working.

open.note:
Doc 22 item 9, and the appearance change that does NOT change identity: it is still THE ASSAY OFFICE, so it is one object with two states rather than the coach's two hotspots with opposite gates. The bounds widen by the swung leaf, which is why per-state bounds exist -- hit-testing the shut door's rect after it opens is the kind of wrongness nobody reports because it nearly works.

THE LEAF IS NOT DRAWN, AND THE BOUNDS ARE THE DOOR'S OWN (2026-09-05, Room 5's Act I pass). The open state used to carry `room-02-assay-door-open.png` -- a 320x144 overlay cut from the composed facade errata 54 discarded (doc 36 Q20's void table) -- and bounds in that space, [1752,300,120,192]. Drawn, the overlay stretched across the whole 3700px plate as a smear beside the hotel; hit-tested, the bounds put the door in the middle of the road, so after the first pass through it the door could not be clicked where it is drawn and Room 5 could not be re-entered from the street. The state still turns on transit (the probe reports it), so the appearance change has a place to land when a leaf exists at plate scale; until then the door looks shut and works. Authoring that leaf is an art operation Tyler authorizes, not a fix.

overrides.PUSH: It opens inward, and it opens easily. Somebody has oiled it.
overrides.CLOSE: It closes itself, slowly, and latches. Somebody sees to that.
overrides.TALK_TO: I have tried talking to it. The building is not the problem.

exits.name: THE HOTEL
exits.note: Doc 20: the hotel is one of the six facades. Stub until doc 14 covers it, as it did not cover the assay office until Room 5 was written.

walkBoxes.note: ERRATA 28a: fixed at the far drawn size, and that is where Room 2's scaling snap now lives. The boardwalk lip is the only real horizontal interruption in the walkable band -- measured at a mean luminance step of 64.5 against 16.3 for the next strongest row -- so stepping off it into the mud is where the sprite swaps from the drawn far sheet to a decimated one. Before boxes the height was one curve across the whole floor and the swap landed at y109, in open mud.

walkBoxNote: GENERATED by tools/compile-room.mjs from reference/room-02-candidate/annotation.json. Heights come from that annotation’s own depth curve, which each room derives from its own architecture -- doc 36 Q10.

occlusionPlanes.note: PHASE 1.5G: CUT FROM THE ART, not drawn round it (tools/retrofit/phase15g-masks.py, plane-1-cut.json). The trough is segmented from the plate's own pixels and trimmed at its base line, so the mask hugs the object and the contact shadow -- which is ground, not an occluder -- is not in it; the rail is its three members as quads, because that is exactly what the rail is. One file, one source of occlusion for both.

occlusionNote: No box in this room is clipPlane 0. Doc 22 defines 0 as always-in-front and nothing in Main Street is nearer than the wagon wheel, whose base sits on the bottom row of the frame -- so there is no depth for such a box to occupy. Recorded rather than left to look like an oversight.

atmosphere.note: ERRATA 33b. Rows 0-20 only: the false fronts reach into the top third, so measuring 'above the horizon' would grade the facades against themselves.
atmosphere.skylineNote: The terrace, the ridges and the steeple -- everything that meets the sky. The mud below the boardwalk is ground, not skyline.

onEnter.note: His first sight of the town, and the words come from doc 05's THE FALSE FRONTS rather than being written fresh -- he has the opinion already; this is him having it out loud at the moment he first has it. AMENDED AFTER TYLER CHECKED IT AGAINST THE PLATE: the original said EVERY building was a false front, which the picture contradicts -- the saloon is a flat parapet with a low roof behind it, and the hotel beside it is genuinely two storeys with lit windows and real depth. The plate is signed off, so the writing yields, and the observation is better for it: the half that is real is the half with money, which is the town's whole economy in one line. Gated on T_SEEN_MAIN_STREET, which onEnter sets, so it plays once.
say: Half of it is two stories tall in front and one story deep.
The other half is real, and is doing better.

generated.note: GENERATED. Edit the documents or the annotation, never this file.

entrances.note: the east edge, by the road in, facing down the street

PHASE 1.5I: 620 -> 592, up onto the boardwalk, x untouched. The saloon door is dead centre of the hitching rail's span, so the mud he used to arrive on is behind the rail -- and that ground is gone. He now steps out of the Nugget onto its own pavement, which is where a man leaving a saloon stands. `arrivalBySource` still says 2317,624; nothing reads it (the compiler uses `entrances`) and it is left alone rather than half-corrected.

lamps.note: the batwing doors and both porch lanterns: the brightest place on the street
the assay office's one lantern over its door
the small lantern by the Clarion's door

occlusionProofs.note: behind the trough, above its base line: its far rim and body mask his feet

frontOnly.note: PHASE 1.5I, TYLER'S RULING: THAD WALKS ONLY IN FRONT OF THIS RAIL. Dual-side navigation is retired -- 1.5G gave the rear ground back, 1.5H made the fence uncrossable, and Tyler could still put him in the rail, because the rear strip mud_mid_3 (x 2268-2614, y 690-776) was legal ground and standing there IS standing in the fence. `rect` is the ground that is no longer player ground: the whole rear of the rail's span, from the top of the far mud (600) down to the top of the front band (816). It is not an overlay the router may route around -- the compiler carves it out, so no walk box exists there at all. `resolveBelowY` is the line a click inside `rect` resolves BELOW: the engine restricts the landing to boxes at or under it, so a click on the bar, on a post, or on the ground behind them puts him on the nearest FRONT-side ground rather than sending him round the block to the boardwalk. `posts` are the two footprints his feet must clear by `minPostClearance`; the far post's foot is at 812 and the front band starts at 816, which is 4 px, so its safety notch carries the front ground down to 824 there. tools/gauntlet/rail-front-only.mjs clicks all of this like a player and asserts he is never inside `rect`.

navigation.note: PHASE 1.5I: `barriers` is gone. It stated the 1.5H contract -- a fence with walkable ground on both sides that may not be crossed between its ends -- and that design is retired: there is no rear side to cross to. What remains is `frontOnly`, which says the stronger thing.
